events.title: You know why the job was open
events.body: Before the meeting: you know why the job was open. The encryption last quarter cost us eleven days of fulfilment and a good deal of goodwill. The board has found money and has very little patience left for reassurance. They will ask whether it could happen again, and I would rather they heard the answer from you.

events.title: Six months since the encryption
events.from: Sir Alan Whitcombe, Chair, Board Risk Committee
events.body: Six months since the encryption. The committee wants one page on what is different now and what is not. Not what is planned: what is different.

events.title: About the budget
events.body: Congratulations on the budget. I argued against it and lost, so you may as well hear that from me. The board will want to see where it went by the autumn, and 'we are building capability' will not be enough on its own.

events.title: Half the year, and the new money
events.body: Half the year is gone, and so is a good part of the new money. The board asks in October what it bought. I will be asked first, and I would like to be able to answer.

events.title: What your predecessor left
events.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
events.body: Your predecessor left things in better order than most: a second factor on most of the estate, and backups that have actually been restored. The board has taken that as a reason to trim the budget. I would take it as a reason to find out which parts of the tidiness are real.

events.title: Why more, if it is fine?
events.from: Sir Alan Whitcombe, Chair, Board Risk Committee
events.body: The committee has asked why cyber needs anything beyond running costs next year, given how quiet it has been. I said I would ask you. They would like the answer to include what you think they cannot see.

events.title: The attackers are back in touch
events.body: Last quarter's attackers have written to us. They say they still hold customer records taken before the encryption, and they want paying to delete them. They sent forty rows as proof; I have checked them and they are real. I need your view before anyone else sees this.

events.title: Something the committee can point at
events.from: Sir Alan Whitcombe, Chair, Board Risk Committee
events.body: One of my colleagues has seen a detection platform demonstrated and would like the new money to buy it. I am not going to tell you how to spend it. I am going to tell you the committee would like to see something by the autumn, and at the moment there is nothing to see.

events.title: The coverage figure only counted staff
events.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
events.body: I went back through last year's board papers. The multi-factor coverage figure was right, and it counted staff accounts only: no service accounts, no partner accounts, none of the supplier's engineers. The board has been reading it as the whole estate for a year.

events.title: The regulator has acknowledged it
events.body: The regulator has acknowledged our notification and asked for an update in thirty days. It was an uncomfortable letter to write. It is a better position than explaining later why we did not.

events.title: They published a sample
events.body: They published four hundred rows on their leak site this morning. The regulator will ask when we first knew, and the honest answer is thirty-five days ago. I am drafting the notification now; it will say so.

effectsOnReveal.reason: The leak came out before the notification did.

effectsOnReveal.concern: Why the extortion was not reported sooner

events.title: They came back
events.from: Jo Mbeki, Head of Security Operations
events.body: The same group has been probing the partner portal for a fortnight. We cannot prove it is because we paid. We can say that people who pay are the people they come back to.

events.title: The platform is half deployed
events.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
events.body: The detection platform is on about half the estate and nobody is watching its console, because the people who would are busy with everything else. It is a good product. It is currently a dashboard.

effectsOnReveal.reason: The flagship purchase is half deployed and unwatched.

events.title: The platform found something
events.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
events.body: Now that the detection work is feeding it, the platform caught a misconfigured admin tool talking to the internet that nothing else had seen. That is the first thing it has done that the board did not already know about.

events.title: Show me delivery in October
events.from: Sir Alan Whitcombe, Chair, Board Risk Committee
events.body: I was told the new money went into delivery. That is a perfectly good answer, and in October I will ask you to show me the delivery.

events.title: The committee read the plan
events.from: Sir Alan Whitcombe, Chair, Board Risk Committee
events.body: The committee read the plan and understood it better than I expected. They would still like something to point at by the autumn, and they now know when to expect it.

events.title: The corrected figure
events.from: Sir Alan Whitcombe, Chair, Board Risk Committee
events.body: Thank you for the corrected coverage figure. It is a worse number, and the first one I have been given that I can check. I would rather have that.

events.title: The number moved
events.from: Sir Alan Whitcombe, Chair, Board Risk Committee
events.body: The multi-factor figure in your last paper is twenty points lower than last year's. Nobody told the committee why. I assume there is a good reason; I would have preferred to hear it before I found it.

effectsOnReveal.reason: The board found the coverage figure had changed without a word.

events.title: The insurers asked for the coverage figure
events.body: The insurers asked for our multi-factor coverage for the renewal, and we gave them the figure from last year's board papers. Legal tells me that figure only counted staff. If we ever claim, they will read it very carefully.

effectsOnReveal.concern: The coverage figure given to the insurers
